mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that increases discount rates for equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals labor market tightness that increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE falls below 4.0%, or the mean return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits above 1.5 million units signals strong household demand and rising inflationary pressure, which triggers a hawkish monetary policy response, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1500.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 103.0 indicates weakening real economic activity, which triggers a dovish policy response and reduces equity risk premiums, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when INDPRO falls below 103.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signal a broad-based demand surge that accelerates inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain high rates, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both RSAFS and HOUST rise, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in CPI inflation above 3.2% combined with a stable federal funds rate signals that inflation expectations are becoming entrenched, which increases long-term real rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.2 and FEDFUNDS is stable, or the interaction signal fails to produce a significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market that is both expanding and tightening, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or the joint signal fails to generate a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) at a quarterly rate above 2.5% signals strong underlying demand growth, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 exceeds 2.5%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
